question: GQ-001
subject: two suites wanted opposite things from the same repo, and my threshold could satisfy only one

the_bind.gate_self_test: builds a 2-commit scratch repo and NEEDS evaluate-refresh to EVALUATE, so its backdated-ledger case can detect staleness
the_bind.load_bearing_suite: builds a 2-commit scratch repo and NEEDS evaluate-refresh to SKIP, or every trigger fires and the baseline fails
the_bind.same_shape_opposite_requirement: no commit-count threshold can satisfy both

two_thresholds_that_each_broke_a_suite.first: < 10 commits — made the gate self-test skip, 5 cases reported GATE DID NOT FIRE
two_thresholds_that_each_broke_a_suite.second: == 1 commit — let the load-bearing baseline fire every trigger, BASELINE FAILED in 21s

the_real_signal_is_commit_WIDTH.measured: real commits here touch 4, 7, 8 files; a scratch import commit touches 531 — the whole repo
the_real_signal_is_commit_WIDTH.why_it_is_the_right_property: a commit that rewrites everything cannot distinguish "this path changed" from "this path exists", which is exactly what makes the history unusable
the_real_signal_is_commit_WIDTH.rule: root commit touching more than half the tracked files = an import, not a history

and_the_self_test_setup_changed_too: its scratch repo now commits ONE file first, then everything else — a narrow root commit gives the gate a history it can reason about, instead of demanding the gate ignore a defect
